original_value: Since the control system in a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) has uncertainties and disturbances, the switching gain is a key factor in effecting chattering in sliding mode control. An adaptive switching gain is proposed for complementary sliding mode control (CSMC) to regulate the PMSM velocity. The proposed switching gain is designed according to system uncertainties. When the value of the sliding modulus is outside the boundary layer, it is positive, resulting in an increase in the switching gain. Conversely, when it is negative, the gain is decreasing. Further, the proposed law considers an arbitrary small vicinity of the sliding manifold, in which the derivatives of the adaptive switching gains are inversely proportional to the sliding modulus to speed up the gain adjustment process. The proposed gain for complementary sliding mode control is applied to regulate the PMSM velocity; comparisons of experimental results show that the proposed gain has a faster gain adjustment process than CSMC and alleviates chattering, resulting in a greater velocity accuracy.

result.paraphrase: Because the control system of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is subject to uncertainties and disturbances, the switching gain is crucial in producing chattering in sliding mode control. To regulate PMSM speed, an adaptive switching gain is introduced for complementary sliding mode control (CSMC). The proposed gain is formulated in line with system uncertainties. When the sliding modulus lies outside the boundary layer, it is positive and the switching gain increases; when it is negative, the gain decreases. The proposed law also accounts for an arbitrarily small neighborhood of the sliding manifold, where the adaptive gain derivatives are inversely proportional to the sliding modulus to accelerate gain adjustment. Applied to PMSM speed regulation, the proposed gain for complementary sliding mode control is shown by experimental comparisons to adjust faster than CSMC, reduce chattering, and achieve higher speed accuracy.
